title: How do parallel sides give three angles on a line?
description: Two angles have sides parallel to the sides of two angles of forty five and seventy eight degrees. Corresponding and vertically opposite angles give two of the three angles on a straight line, and the third is the rest of one hundred and eighty degrees.
teaching_notes: One idea: an angle with sides parallel to another angle has the same size, and angles on a straight line add up to one hundred and eighty degrees. Watch for students who forget to take away both angles.

video_script.why: The child carries equal angles across parallel sides and then uses the straight line, as in the solved example, to find the remaining angle.
video_script.substitution: the book's own figure: angle ABC is forty five degrees, angle IKJ is seventy eight degrees, and the rays EH and EF go up from the line G E D in the order G, H, F, D
video_script.anchor: angle ABC marked 45° and angle IKJ marked 78°, and a straight line G E D with the rays EH and EF going up from E in the order G, H, F, D
video_script.payoff_line: The three angles fit together on the straight line

final_answer.value: Angle GEH = 45°, angle HEF = 57°, angle FED = 78°
final_answer.spoken: angle G E H is forty five degrees, angle H E F is fifty seven degrees, and angle F E D is seventy eight degrees

hold_back: Angle GEH = 45°, angle HEF = 57°, angle FED = 78°
maths_rules: angle GEH has sides parallel to the sides of angle ABC, and it is the corresponding angle and then the vertically opposite angle, so angle GEH = 45
angle FED has sides parallel to the sides of angle IKJ, in the same way, so angle FED = 78
G, E and D lie on a straight line, so angle GEH + angle HEF + angle FED = 180
video_script.design: The two given angles on the left and the straight line with two rays on the right. The equal angles take matching colours, and the angle that is found takes a third colour.
